header.name: Industrial Organization (IO)
header.description: This course will introduce basic theoretical models of IO. It will implement applied microenomic theory and game theory to understand how firms take decisions in various settings. The models include profir maximization when there is market power, advertising, heterogeneity in quality, vertical control, models of entry, accomodation and exit, and many others. The course helps one understand how to set up an objective function for a firm facing different challenges in a complex market structure. It will aid the student in understanding real world scenarios. Finally there will also be a short section on some empirical methods used in IO. IO has grown into one of the fundamental fields within economics, and is essential in order to gain a broader understanding of the subject.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Identifying how to approach a problem in IO in a strategic setting

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Determining how to model decision that influence profit, like advertising, quality, collusion etc.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Discussing decisions in monopolies, duopolies, vertical control.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Justifying and explaining what motivates a firm to enter or exit a market.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Identifying and Implementing some basic empirical and applied theory techniques in IO (for 5XX).
